I think a lot of people in the debate about the Federal Reserve (on both sides) don't understand just how much our monetary system - especially since the 80s - relies on debt. Let's say you go to buy a TV at one of those places with "no payments for 2 years!". A lender (bank) will borrow money from the Federal Reserve to lend to you to buy the TV. The TV manufacturers are happy, since they get the money right away. You're happy, because you have a TV. The bank is happy, because the first thing they do is package up your loan into a CDO and sell it off to a hedge fund (who has investors that are mutual funds/pension plans, and ultimately your retirement account), so they're not taking any of the risk of you not paying. If in 2 years you can't pay, you can refinance or take a HELOC to help pay for it -- therefore borrowing more money. The very same hedge fund might buy the CDO for the funds you refinanced with -- meaning they're essentially paying interest to themselves. Banks/investors are often leveraged 40:1 or greater -- meaning they have 40x as much debt as they have assets.

Given that, switching back to money representing some real, tangible goods -- typically gold or silver -- would upend the entire existing financial structure. I'm not saying it would be a bad thing or a good thing, but it would mean middle class and poor would have a LOT less credit available. Banks would be much less willing to give you a credit card or lend you money to buy a house. It would also stifle innovation on projects/companies that need a lot of investment, significantly decreasing America's competitiveness in sectors like technology.

The winners of a switch to a gold/silver standard -- at least in the short term -- would be the people who are already rich in industries other than banking/finance. If you own some oil wells, a hospital, or a chain of fast food restaurants, you would be sitting pretty. The losers would be the poor and middle class who live beyond their means on credit cards and loans. And banking/finance would of course fall apart. Basically, the rich would get richer and the poor would get poorer.

Think about everything you've bought on credit in the last month, and every piece of property you owe money on (your car, your house, etc). If that list is empty, you would benefit from switching away from the federal reserve system (in the short term). If not, then you would suffer.

Daily Devotional

October 11

19 We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed, as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts: 20 Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. - 2 Peter 1:19-20 (KJV)

 Peter had been making it known that he was about to come to the end of his life (2 Peter 1:14), and had been relaying to the saints, all that he had witnessed when he was with Jesus for three and one-half years. Now Peter is saying that even though he had heard the audible voice of God (2 Peter 1:18), and saw Jesus transfigured on the mount, there was even a greater witness than that. Most people would say, what could be greater than hearing the voice of God, but what Peter is telling us, is that the written word of God is more sure than any verbal, physical or feeling, that we could ever have. Most humans want something physical to see, feel, hear, taste or touch, but Peter is telling us that the written scriptures are more sure than anything we could ever experience with our five senses.

 We are so blessed to have the written scriptures in the bible, to study and learn the things of God. Also we have the Holy Ghost to help us understand the scriptures (John 14:26), and make them come alive to us as we read them. No one could teach us better than the Holy Spirit, as He is the one that inspired the prophets to write the books of the bible, so He is teaching us His words. Our understanding of the things of God, are so much better than any of the disciples that lived with Jesus could have. We have all their perspectives together, and the one that wrote the majority of the New Testament, was Paul, who did not walk with Jesus during His ministry. Praise God for the bible, and the Holy Spirit to teach it to us!

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
